questions.q: Which of the three protocols in SQL Server Configuration Manager is required for any remote network connection?
options: TCP/IP
Named Pipes, exclusively
Shared Memory
None — remote connections don't require any specific protocol
questions.explain: TCP/IP is the standard protocol required for remote connections; Shared Memory only works for local connections on the same machine.

questions.q: What happens if TCP/IP shows Disabled in Configuration Manager for an instance?
options: Only Named Pipes connections are affected
Local connections also stop working entirely
It has no effect on connectivity at all
No remote client can connect over the network, regardless of firewall rules or SQL Server Browser
questions.explain: If TCP/IP is disabled at the protocol level, remote connections fail entirely no matter what the firewall or Browser configuration looks like — the protocol itself is off.

questions.q: What does the TCP Dynamic Ports setting do?
options: Lets SQL Server pick an available port at startup, which can change between restarts
Only applies to default instances, never named instances
Disables TCP/IP entirely
Permanently fixes the port to 1433 for every instance
questions.explain: TCP Dynamic Ports is the default for named instances — SQL Server selects an available port at startup, and that value can change on a subsequent restart.

questions.q: Why might a DBA deliberately configure a static port for a named instance?
options: To make firewall rules and connection strings predictable and stable across restarts
Static ports automatically improve query performance
Named instances cannot use SQL Server Browser unless a static port is set
Static ports are required by SQL Server licensing
questions.explain: A fixed port trades away some automatic convenience for operational predictability — firewall rules and connection strings don't have to account for a port that might change.

questions.q: What must happen after enabling TCP/IP in Configuration Manager for the change to take effect?
options: The Database Engine service must be restarted
SQL Server Agent must be restarted, not the Database Engine
The entire Windows Server must be rebooted
The change takes effect immediately with no restart needed
questions.explain: Enabling or changing the TCP/IP protocol requires restarting the Database Engine service — it isn't a live change like some other Configuration Manager settings.
